key_insight: TEDDY is a compact pediatric foundation model that learns from ICD-coded diagnosis histories to forecast future disease risk and visit timing.
clinical_relevance: It could help identify children at elevated risk for common and rare conditions earlier than traditional models, potentially supporting earlier follow-up and monitoring.
method: Trained a 1.84M-parameter decoder transformer on ~73 million ICD-10 diagnoses from 1.6 million children.
Modeled longitudinal diagnosis trajectories and visit timing using first-occurrence, pre-visit prediction settings.
Compared performance against sex- and age-matched controls and multiple same-data baselines, including DenseNet, CNN, RNN, and LSTM.
evidence_signal: Across 797 disease-onset tasks, TEDDY achieved a median AUC of 72.0% and outperformed baselines on 96-99% of tasks; it also predicted asthma and ADHD with AUCs of 79.3% and 84.7%.
watch_item: This is a single-institution retrospective study, so generalizability, calibration over long return intervals, and real-world workflow impact still need prospective validation.
paper_title: TEDDY: A Pediatric Foundation Model for Risk Forewarning from ICD-Coded Diagnostic Histories
